title: Dynamic Cost Safeguard: Prompt Anchors & Canary Eval Harness for Safe Batch/Cache Policies
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight canary evaluation harness and policy gating system that lets the autoscaling/auto-apply service propose batching and KV-cache configuration changes and only apply them after passing signal checks tied to a small, representative set of 'prompt anchors' and canary traffic. Focus is on reducing token cost while preventing semantic regressions and user-visible quality drops.
acceptance_criteria: Canary harness runs automatically for proposed batch/cache policy changes and produces a pass/fail signal based on defined thresholds
Prompt anchors (10-25 items) cover high-risk intents: instruction collapsing, structured output tables, code snippets, and short/long context edge cases
Acceptance thresholds defined for answer-stability (>=0.92), semantic-similarity (SBERT >=0.88), and latency/cost delta bounds (cost <= -5% and p95 latency <= +10%)
If any anchor fails, policy changes are blocked and a rollback ticket is auto-created with diffs and suggested safer profile
Playbook documents for manual override, emergency rollback, and stakeholder notifications exist and are linked in the run output
design_decisions: Use 'prompt anchors' (human-curated representative prompts) instead of a single golden prompt to increase robustness against paraphrase and distribution shift
Compute two orthogonal regression signals: semantic-similarity (SBERT cosine) and answer-stability (token-level exact-match + normalized edit distance) to reduce false positives
Run canary on a small dedicated pool (5-10% of traffic) and on synthetic replay of recorded production traces to detect regressions that only appear under longer contexts
Prefer conservative rollout: require all critical anchors to pass or require supervisor approval for single-anchor failures with high cost savings
Store canary results and embeddings to S3 for auditability and to seed future anchor selection automation
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff with PM and SRE. Agreed on anchor families and initial metric suite (stability, sbert, cost, latency).

2026-02-18: Prototype runner implemented (python) to load candidate policy, run anchors, compute SBERT embeddings, and generate HTML diff report. Local tests on internal rollouts passed basic smoke tests.
2026-02-25: Integration spike with autoscaler service: created a proposal schema for policy diffs and canary metadata. Identified need for a short-lived canary pool API (ENG spike required).
2026-03-03: UX sync with Console team to surface canary results in rollout UI. Decided to include a single-click 'block & create rollback' button and attach run artifacts.

2026-03-08: Pilot run against 'small-batch-8' policy on staging with 20 anchors. Observed one anchor failing answer-stability for code-generation snippets; cost delta -6.7%, p95 latency +3%. Flagged for review.

2026-03-11: Postmortem on failing anchor: found that continuous-batching changed token alignment for code fences causing minor formatting changes. Decision: add normalization step for code tokens and tighten similarity weighting.
reviewer_feedback: PM (Jordan Lee): Good scope; require a PM signoff threshold param to allow targeted teams to opt-in before global policy apply.
SRE (Nina Gomez): Add canary pool isolation and quota so canary traffic doesn't affect capacity or SLAs.
Research (Dr. Evan Cho): Recommend adding a paraphrase-robustness check using multiple SBERT encoders and a small generation-based equivalence test for structured outputs.
Security (Priya Raman): Request for an audit log entry on every auto-apply action and retention of anchor inputs behind access controls — added to playbook.
next_steps: Finalize anchor set (target 18 anchors) and add normalization pipeline for code/markdown outputs (owner: Marco)
Implement canary pool API and quota enforcement (owner: SRE team lead)
Wire canary runner into autoscaler proposal flow and add automatic 'block & rollback' rule based on thresholds
Add a small UI card in Console rollout page to display per-anchor metrics and raw diffs (owner: Console UX)
Run a 1-week staging pilot with traffic split and an escalation cadence; capture lessons and adjust thresholds before release
